trails.title: The Killing Board
trails.description: Black and white pieces land; the scales of attack and defense change hands.

content.text:
[Opening: French Defense]
...
25. White: Queen d2 | Black: Queen e4 [Black breaks through White's queenside.]
Krutov: "Those Foundation office rats don't know the first thing about combat. Keep the pressure on the front lines! Push forward!"
26. White: Queen xg5+ | Black: Queen g6 [Black's kingside is exposed—White's queen strikes.]
Krutov: "What in the hell are those people in the back doing with their arcane skills? ... Never mind them—more firepower! Tear a hole in this line!"
27. White: Rook xg6+ | Black: fxg6 [White presses the attack against Black.]
Krutov: "Hold the line until reinforcements arrive ... What are the 'orchestra' and those 'gatekeepers' doing?"

[Middlegame: Kingside Storm]
...
31. White: Bishop xg6 | Black: Knight d5 [White clears the queenside—the tide turns.]
Krutov: "Where are the reinforcements? Where the hell are they!"
32. White: Queen xb7 | Black: King xg6 [White's pieces strike back at Black.]
Krutov: "Say that again—what do you mean, 'The traitor has destroyed the main channel of our network'?! Where the hell are Lyra and that pile of scrap metal?"
33. White: Queen xa8 | Black: Knight xc3 [Black's pawns make a desperate last stand.]
Krutov: "Where do you think you're going! There's no retreat! Stick to the plan! Break through their last line of defense!"

[Endgame: Battle for the Post]
...
46. White: Queen b2 | Black: King d1 [Black risks it all on promotion.]
Krutov: "There's nowhere to go but forward—so fight like your lives depend on it! Keep tearing through these Foundation scum!"
47. White: Queen xc3 | Black: c1=Queen [Black pawn promotes to Queen.]
Krutov: "She will come for us! Hold the line!"
...

items.text: Song of the Black Sheep
Countdown to the "Storm"

items.speaker: Lyra
items.text: Prima, should the language of music elude you, you may command them with incantations in its stead.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Yes, ma'am.

items.speaker: Lyra
items.text: I have matters to attend to whilst you children play your games with the Foundation. I trust the "Windweave" will be safe in your care.

items.speaker: Lyra
items.text: You may one day be worthy of your mother's place. But first, prove yourself.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I said, be quiet!
She holds herself up against the building's coarse outer wall.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: So many donned this mask because of your lies. Do you remember their faces?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: -227,110#You lured them in, broke them, and cast them into the abyss, stood by and watched them surrender their souls to a goddess you never believed in—never truly knew.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I did.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text:
178,104#Now it's your turn to face the trial. You know what awaits you if you fail.

                                                                    Why not seek the forgiveness of the Mother of Resurrection?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: 31,-19#She has spared you. She would embrace you once more, as any loving mother would a wayward child.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I won't. I'll never return to her.
She staggers back to her feet.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: This mask can't overpower me. I know how to control it.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: -259,68#Of course. You are no stranger to this mask. You've worn it before. But then, you still had the Phototaxis to protect you.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: 516,-50#How daring of you to think you can master it alone this time.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: At least my mind is still my own. That's all I need.
Her attention is drawn to the southernmost building.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: That way is Building 5, where the refugees were housed.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: 0,0#And do you see those people? Arcanist soldiers—our brothers and sisters—they have put on the mask. From this day forth, they fight only for their own people.
A gray and white tower stands not far off. Soldiers in black exit onto the path leading to the Foundation headquarters.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Those are Krutov's troops. Prima's memory was correct. That must be where the Manus entered the Foundation.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: But why here? Why in the refugees' residences?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Let's find out, shall we?
Bold strides carry her through throngs of Arcana's followers and toward Building 5.
Nobody pays the masked woman any mind.
She slips through the door and enters the building.
Entrance, Building Five
It isn't that she expected to see anything in particular. She hasn't given it enough time to expect anything at all. But the sight that greets her still exceeds her wildest imagination.
Mycelia-like bodies playing bizarre music quiver in the air, their steady yet creeping movements resembling the closing mouths of Venus flytraps.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: This is ...

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: A passage that connects us all.
Using limbs mutated into instruments, believers twist and writhe their bodies in resonance with the "Windweave's" deep tones.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: This must be the orchestra Lyra mentioned, and these monsters are communicating through song. This is where they sent those who failed the trial.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: When and how did Lyra do all this? I had no idea. I must have overlooked some clue.
She suppresses her guilt and focuses her attention on the strange maw's depths instead.
From the location of its "throat" emerges another troop of shadowy figures.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: I'm sure you know what must be done.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Yes. I will end it here.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I know how to control these things, and Prima has just shown me the incantation to command them.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I'll order the orchestra to play the song to sever the "Windweave."

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Hmph!

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I'll just—Urgh!
The mask gnaws at her consciousness. The hands covering her face are like delicate instruments of torture, peeling the nonbeliever's disguise away layer by layer.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Did it ever occur to you, in all the grandness of your mission, that using a Manus incantation might invite the mask deeper into your mind?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Your resistance is as pathetic as it is ungrateful in the face of the Guiding One's mercy.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Come along home, dear. Lay down that heavy burden. You're no Foundation dog. You're with your own kind. You'll be safe. You can finally be free.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: You've been away for far too long. Too long to remember what it is to belong, to be happy, to be surrounded by family. Come back. We will all rejoice in your return.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: You can have the life you want and a new name. Not "Grace," not "Moth," no longer a "Stranger."

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Go   home,   to   the   primeval   glaciers.
An incantation is chanted. The piercing hum bores through her eyeballs and into her brain like a fanged worm, devouring the tender flesh in its path.
Her limbs tremble, as if her own body were joining the sickening orchestra.
Amid all the chaos, she hears it—the orchestra's melody is changing.
The final note plays, and in that instant, she faintly hears a prolonged wail of agony coming from the abyss.
A force wraps around the sound like a gentle cover before whisking it away into the recesses of a far-off time.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: It's done. The portal is closed.
The incantation worked. She knows she's succeeded. Yet her success will come at a price.
Without control over the Phototaxis, she is powerless to resist the mask's trial.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: No. Don't do this to me. No!

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I don't ... want to ... go ...

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: No more names ... No more orders ...

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I've ... never ... really lived ... ㄜ ...

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Harrrgh! *cough*

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: *vomit*

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I want to live.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: To leave here.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: To never, never come back.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Fighting on foot? Ugh. You gotta be kidding me.
Lilya gives a disheartened look over to her inert broom. She won't be returning to the sky for now.

But she can't make clear sense of why. It seemed that her Red 38's arcane engine stalled all at once and for no clear reason. The conclusion only comes to her as she realizes she's lost her arcane skills as well.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Looks like I need to leave you here, buddy. Better hope the Manus don't snatch you up.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hello?
But she still has a pistol.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Who's there?
A figure staggers into view, only noticeable when she's come close enough for Lilya to make out her face.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Help, help.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: It's you! You—
She catches Ms. Stranger as she sinks to her knees.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You're all covered in slime. What the hell happened?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: The portal ... The Manus's portal is closed.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Mission complete.
